newsitem.title: RUSSIA: RUSSIAN DIAMOND MINER PLANS EUROBOND.
newsitem.headline: RUSSIAN DIAMOND MINER PLANS EUROBOND.

text.p: Russia's main diamond producer Almazy Rossii-Sakha (ARS), which is about to sign an agreement with South African diamond giant De Beers , plans to tap international bond markets this year to fund the development of its mines.
"We are preparing a Eurobond project and propose issuing a Eurobond by the end of the year," vice-president Semyon Zelberg told Reuters.
ARS intends to issue a $100 million Eurobond this year, and if that is successful will become a regular borrower to fund its diamond mines, he said.
"If we start with $100 million in 1997, later the volume of borrowing may grow up to $300 million annually," Zelberg said.
In 1996 ARS produced about $1.35 billion worth of rough diamonds.
Last year ARS mandated Britain's National Westmister Bank Plc to arrange a $500 million loan to finance exploration and development.
But the bank shelved the project until Russia and De Beers concluded talks on the long-delayed marketing agreement.

De Beers, which controls the world's diamond trade, sharply curtailed its purchases of Russian diamonds at the end of last year when Moscow failed to communicate its position on a draft agreement submitted to the cabinet in October 1996.
Russia's First Deputy Prime Minister Anatoly Chubais said this month the agreement will be signed no later than June 4.
ARS will have an annual export quota of at least $550 million under the new agreement, ARS spokesman Yuri Beskakotov said.
Russia will have the right to sell five percent of the quota itself to monitor market conditions, he told Reuters.
Under the long-delayed agreement Russia will also be allowed to directly export additional diamonds outside the quota to the value of 25 percent of the quota, he said.
Russian diamonds accounted for 26 percent of De Beers's total worldwide sales under the previous contract, a deal worth about $1.2 billion a year to Russia.

Zelberg said ARS planned to name two lead managers for the Eurobond project on May 20. Apart from National Westminster, SBC Warburg, Salomon Brothers and Smith Barney are bidding for the mandate for the Eurobond, one of several now being planned by Russian companies, he said.
